messages.subject: [rhipe] map/reduce key sorting
parts:
Hadoop sorts the key/value pairs between the map and the reduce and
I've noticed in the wordcount example in Rhipe that the keys are
indeed sorted before being written to the sequence file. However it
doesn't sort when I am using numbers. I was wondering what the
default settings were and if anyone has had any success getting it to
sort numbers.

I am trying to do this by adding the following as part of my rhmr(...)
call:

mapred=list(mapred.text.key.partitioner.options="-k1n")

which from what I understand, should sort the keys by the first part,
as numbers.

I realize that this may be more of a Hadoop question than Rhipe
specifically but I am not too familiar with either.

messages.author: 5b0c9158bfa781ba
messages.subject: Re: [rhipe] map/reduce key sorting
parts:
When it comes to sorting you might be in trouble. Nothing is text in Rhipe -
everything from reading in data, sending to the map, from map to reduce(thus
including the shuffling and sorting) is done using binary bytes and all
comparisons are are byte sequence comparisons

So text e.g "field1 field2" is written out as

08 00 2a 0f 0a 0d 66 69 65 6c 64 31 20 66 69 65 6c 64 32

and indeed these might preserve lexicographic sorting(assuming string lengths
are not varint encoded) - but I've never checked for this.

So your keys are numbers? Numbers ought to sort, but I don't know (and doubt)
that numerical order will be preserved when the byte representations(protocol
buffer) are compared.

> mapred=list(mapred.text.key.partitioner.options="-k1n")

Will probably not work since there is never any text writable used (except for
reading in text files, but not between map and reduce)

Adding in custom partitioners (e.g. partition on the first element of an atomic string vector) though possible, would probably slow things down a lot. Still it is a good idea to have as an option.

Regards
Saptarshi

messages.subject: Re: [rhipe] Re: map/reduce key sorting
parts:
Hello,
Apologies for the long delay, I've been trying to fix some papers.


>After comparing many serialized numbers and char strings, serializing
>does indeed preserve lexicographic ordering.

Still surprising.


>However I am noticing that sorting is not occurring at all, contrary
>to what I stated earlier.  I believe I was testing on too small of a
>sample before and it just happened to have sorted them correctly. It
>seems that at some level Hadoop must do some sorting to collect k/v
>pairs with the same keys but I am not too sure what is going on and
>how to force a complete sorting of the keys.

If you look at the raw bytes the keys for a give part** file will be sorted -
the sorting happens on the byte level. If you notice value sorting (as in your
first paragraph) this needs to be proved.


>
>Can you perhaps shed some light on how streaming is called?  The
>streaming doc indicates that there is a secondary sort option for the
>keys.
>
Streaming internals have been re-written, the entire java program uses
RHBytesWritable as key and value. Not a single mention of Double, Integer or
Text. Streaming allows the secondary sort etc because it has a different
partitioner - I have been thinking of implementing a partitioner but this can
cause many surprising side effects.

So to summarize, your keys *are* sorted (Hadoop will do this) but at the byte
level which might not be of any help at the value level.

Regards
Saptarshi
